source.title: Features that Make a Difference: Leveraging Gradients for Improved Dictionary Learning
source.authors: Jeffrey Olmo; J. Wilson; Max Forsey; Bryce Hepner; T. Howe; David Wingate

record.tranche_reason: Measures the change in model loss when SAE reconstructions are propagated through the model, but does not compare them with random errors of matched size.
record.gate_note: The reported loss-added measurements bear on the effect of SAE reconstruction errors. The study does not measure their linear predictability, per-token scaling or context overlap, nor whether retaining the error term preserves behavior. Steering, dead-latent, interpretability and activity-density results do not test those claims.
record.test_reason: The study proposes gradient-aware TopK SAEs (g-SAEs) and reports how they perform against TopK and e2e SAEs on loss added, NMSE, dead latents, steering and interpretability. It never compares SAE reconstruction errors with random errors of matched norm. It does not measure linear predictability of the error, per-token error scaling, or the effect of keeping the error term. Its loss-added rows compare its own method with baselines, so they do not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors conclude that g-SAEs give lower loss added at a given sparsity and expansion size, across GPT-2 sizes. They also conclude that g-SAE latents steer outputs more strongly and more specifically (about 5x the added probability of associated logits versus TopK), with fewer dead latents and no measurable loss of human-rated interpretability. They do not assess error versus matched random error.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces gradient-aware TopK selection in g-SAEs and compares it with TopK and e2e SAE variants; it does not report the dark-matter analyses in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that g-SAE loss-added advantages vary with sparsity and persist across the tested GPT-2 sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: From layer 3 onward in GPT-2 small, directional derivatives of loss along activation-difference directions exceed those along isotropic and covariance-adjusted random directions (Fig. 2). The norm of a random perturbation correlates only weakly with the change in loss, which can vary by up to three orders of magnitude with direction (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model outputs are more locally sensitive to perturbations along feature directions than along random directions, so equal-norm errors differ in downstream harm. This is a candidate mechanism for pathological SAE errors, but is not measured on SAE errors.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched sparsity, g-SAEs have NMSE comparable to TopK but add slightly less cross-entropy loss, on GPT-2 small through xl (Figs. 4, 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How much downstream loss SAE error adds can be partly reduced by the training or selection rule without reducing reconstruction error norm. This relates to V3 and V6 but is not a dark-matter measurement.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No matched random-error comparison for V3; exact plotted values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text. The loss-added findings are on GPT-2 models and do not test error structure or behavioral effects beyond the reported loss measure.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported outcomes—NMSE, dead latents, steering, activity density, feature similarity and human interpretability—do not measure the SAE error comparisons specified by the claim. Relevant loss-added plots are represented by R1–R5.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, overlap of failing contexts, and persistence of error with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction errors raise loss more than random errors of the same norm. The random-direction comparisons use activation differences, not SAE errors.
The split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts, and whether the nonlinear part resists further dictionary learning.
Whether circuit or steering analyses lose behaviour when the error term is dropped.
Whether dark matter mostly reflects training choices. g-SAE changes loss added but no dark-matter decomposition is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its V3 limits_scope label are not justified. A missing comparison is an untested part, not a scope limit, and the rows compare the study's own method with baselines. I reclassified the study as T4 (uses_without_test) with no verdicts. Published at NAACL 2025.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, context overlap across sizes, and whether error persists with scale.
The comparison against random errors of the same size.
The distinction between learned-feature error and nonlinear error, and whether the latter resists further dictionary learning.
Whether analyses lose behavior when the SAE error term is omitted.
Whether dark matter mostly arises from SAE training choices, or whether its structure reflects the model representation.
